findings.F1: Over the next 20 days, a coin's one-day return points the other way, and strongly. The slope of the 20-day excess return (in units of the coin's usual 20-day move) on the ranked one-day return is -0.157 per standard deviation (t -6.1, 1456 non-overlapping cases). It holds when returns are clipped (t -6.3) and when the day's return is scaled by its 20-day volatility (t -5.4).
findings.F2: The book's gain is all on the long side. Long bars earned +0.21 % per bar (17987 bars, sum 38.0), short bars -0.0085 % (18868 bars, sum -1.6). Shorts paid only in falling years (2018 +0.14 %, 2022 +0.11 % per bar) and lost in 2020, 2023 and 2024 (-0.11 % to -0.14 % per bar).
findings.F3: The deepest falls are not where the losses continue, which fits F1. In the forecast's quintiles:
findings.F4: The 28-day momentum effect is larger over 10 days than over the tested 5.
findings.F5: Momentum works in calm markets and fades in volatile ones, but the pattern is not robust enough to act on.
findings.F6: The book's largest days are followed by gains whichever way they went, so they mark volatility, not direction.
findings.F7: Other angles looked at showed nothing to count.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on its last day, the higher its return over the next 20 days, the gain growing with the depth of the day's fall.
ideas.consequence: After a coin's sharp one-day drop, lean long for the following weeks in proportion to the drop rather than short it, and refuse shorts taken right after a deep down day.
ideas.name: Deep down-day weeks-long rebound

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 28-day return, the higher its return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: Hold four-week momentum positions for about two weeks rather than one, since the move keeps building past five days.
ideas.name: Four-week momentum, two-week horizon
